questions.title: Why do legal threats and emotional distress not constitute 'past persecution' under the INth Circuit?
questions.question_body: I am reading the section on 'Past Persecution' and I am confused about the threshold. The court cites Karki and Wiransane saying threat alone is insufficient. But the petitioners suffered physical stress and panic attacks. If donors suffered these, why did the court say threats alone don't equal persecution, even if they are 'unfortunate circumstances'?

questions.title: How does the 'central reason' test distinguish between political opinion and professional conflict in a mixed-motive case?
questions.question_body: In the 'Nexus' section, the court says political opinion cannot be incidental. Jiménez was targeted for investigating a narco base, not just for being in the Liberal party. How do we legally determine when a 'mixed motive' of political affiliation vs. professional involvement (like Don Rafa case) fails to meet the 'on account of protected ground' requirement?

questions.title: Why does the failure to formally report persecution to the government prevent proving the government is 'unable or unwilling' to protect?
questions.question_body: The court cites Aviles-Gonzalez regarding reporting requirements. Jiménez worked for the government and had contacts but didn't report formally. If a law enforcement officer told them to leave during a conversation, why does that not qualify as 'evidence of systemic, rather than individual, failures' to prove the government is 'unable or unwilling'?

questions.title: What specific evidence supports a finding of 'safe internal relocation' if the threat involves high-level narco-trafficking leaders?
questions.question_body: The 'Safe Relocation' section says Petitioners could relocate. They lived in the countryside for 3 weeks. But Don Rafa was associated with the President. Why does a 3-week stay in the countryside sufficient to negate a fear of relocation, and does the presence of family in Colombia always guarantee safety under ICT standards?

questions.title: Why does denying asylum automatically result in denying withholding of removal according to Carias-Mejia?
questions.question_body: In the conclusion, the court says failing asylum standards means failing withholding because withholding is a 'higher standard'. But earlier, the court said asylum is discretionary while withholding is mandatory if a refugee. If asylum is discretionary, why can't someone get withholding if they can't meet Asylum's discretion but meet Withholding's strict fear?

questions.title: How does the 'Administrative Record' restriction limit the 10th Circuit from reviewing the 'Right to Counsel' claims raised in the BIA?
questions.question_body: The petitioners claimed they were denied due process for lack of counsel at the IJ level, but they waived the appeal on this issue and limited their appeal to asylum. The court relies on § 1252(b)(4)(A) to limit review to the administrative record. Since the record doesn't include oral arguments about counsel, how can the court confirm the BIA's factual findings regarding those issues?
